title: Ombudsman suspends mayor of Rosario, Cavite, for alleged casino gambling
summary: The 6-month preventive suspension without pay is a measure to guarantee an unbiased and unhindered administrative investigation, says the Ombudsman

blocks.text: ALLEGED GAMBLING. Rosario, Cavite Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente allegedly left a casino in Bacolod City with four companions and P10,000 worth of winnings.
The 6-month preventive suspension without pay is a measure to guarantee an unbiased and unhindered administrative investigation, says the Ombudsman

The Office of the Ombudsman ordered on Thursday, November 12, the six-month preventive suspension of Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente of Rosario, Cavite, over his alleged engagement in gambling activities at a casino in Bacolod City.

The order stemmed from a complaint filed by the Field Investigation Office (FIO) of the Office of the Ombudsman, which found that Ricafrente, along with four companions, entered the casino at a hotel on March 14, 2026.
The Rosario mayor allegedly played at a gaming table with P30,000 worth of casino chips and won P10,000 before leaving the casino.
Under Presidential Decree No. 1869 or the PAGCOR Charter and Memorandum Circular No. 6 s. 2016, government personnel are strictly prohibited from entering, staying, or playing in casinos.

“This Office finds sufficient grounds for the issuance of an Order for Preventive Suspension against respondent Municipal Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente, Municipality of Rosario, Province of Cavite, considering that there is strong evidence showing his guilt; the charges against him for Grave Misconduct and Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of the Service may warrant his removal from the service,” the six-page order stated.
Ricafrente will be preventively suspended without pay pending the resolution of the administrative charges against him.
The Ombudsman said a preventive suspension is not a penalty but serves as a measure to guarantee an unbiased and unhindered administrative investigation.

Ricafrente is a close ally of the Revilla dysnasty in Cavite. His municipality is within the Cavite 1st District represented by Jolo Revilla. Jose Voltaire is the son of the late former mayor Jose “Nonong” Ricafrente Jr., who served as provincial administrator when Bong Revilla Jr. was governor.
Rappler has reached out to the municipal government and Ricafrente’s office for a statement on the issue. This article will be updated with his reply. – Rappler.com
